Theorem
[Weak maximum principle] Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0191 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0192 1. ch8:8.1\group ch08-generalized-solutions Assume (8.5), (8.6), and (8.8). If $u\in W^{1,2}(\Omega )$ satisfies $Lu\geq 0$ (respectively, $Lu\leq 0$), then \begin{equation} \sup _\Omega u\leq \sup _{\partial \Omega }u^+, \qquad \left(\text{respectively, }\inf _\Omega u\geq \inf _{\partial \Omega }u^-\right). \tag {8.9} \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch It suffices to treat the subsolution case. Put $l=\sup _{\partial \Omega }u^+$ and test with $v=(u-k)^+$ for $l\leq k<\sup _\Omega u$. Condition (8.8), applied to $uv$, removes the zeroth-order contribution, while ellipticity and (8.6) give

\begin{equation} \tag {8.10} \int _\Omega a^{ij}D_j uD_i v\, dx \leq 2\lambda \int _\Omega v|Du|\, dx. \end{equation}

This yields an estimate of $\| Dv\| _2$ by $\| v\| _{L^2(\supp Dv)}$. Sobolev and Hölder inequalities then force $|\supp Dv|$ to have a positive lower bound independent of $k$. Letting $k\uparrow \sup _\Omega u$ contradicts the vanishing of $Du$ on the top level set. Apply the result to $-u$ for the supersolution statement.

□
